name: Andanza
list_view_snippet: A warm Spanish tapas spot on Weston Street serving shareable plates and bold flavours in an intimate, unpretentious setting.
full_profile:
Tucked away on Weston Street, Andanza brings a relaxed, welcoming slice of Spain to Bermondsey. The low-lit, rustic interior feels like a tucked-away secret — perfect for lingering evenings with friends.

The menu focuses on classic and contemporary tapas: think jamón ibérico, garlicky prawns, and patatas bravas with a punchy salsa. Everything is designed for sharing, so expect small plates that arrive as they’re ready, encouraging a slow, sociable meal.

Best for casual dates or after-work catch-ups where you want good wine, bold flavours, and zero pretension. No need to book — just turn up and settle in.

name: Baccalà London
list_view_snippet: A polished, concrete-hued snug celebrating Italian seafood, handmade pasta, and artisanal low-intervention wines, with a unique focus on boutique extra virgin olive oils.
full_profile:
Tucked away on Bermondsey Street, Baccalà is a polished concrete snug that balances industrial chic with a warm, welcoming Mediterranean soul. The atmosphere is intimate and refined, offering a joyous retreat from the city’s bustle where the hospitality is as smooth as the expertly curated sommelier-led service.

The kitchen champions high-end Italian seafood and sustainable seasonal ingredients. Signature offerings include wild bass carpaccio and handmade pasta, though the true star is the executive chef’s focus on artisanal extra virgin olive oil, which is treated with the reverence of fine wine. On Saturdays, the venue transforms into a premier oyster bar featuring premium UK and Irish catches.

It is the ultimate destination for seafood aficionados and curious wine lovers looking to explore Italy’s twenty wine regions. Whether visiting for an 'Italian Wine Tuesday' with 50% off bottles or a sophisticated Saturday afternoon of oysters and bubbles, it delivers an unforgettable and educational dining experience.

name: Café Amisha
list_view_snippet: A welcoming Grange Road sanctuary serving authentic 'Mamma style' Italian classics, market-fresh seafood, and home-baked treats on a charming, sun-soaked terrace.
full_profile:
Located on Grange Road, just a short stroll from the lively Bermondsey Street, Café Amisha offers a neighbourhood atmosphere defined by warmth and simplicity. The setting is relaxed and welcoming, featuring a charming outside terrace that has been a staple for local diners since its opening in 2013. Inside, the environment is intimate and unpretentious, managed by a friendly team dedicated to a memorable dining experience.

The culinary focus is on authentic Italian 'Mamma style' comfort food, with a strict emphasis on quality and freshness. The restaurant bakes its own bread and cakes on-site and sources fish and meat daily from local London markets. Signature offerings include handmade pasta dishes like Tagliatelle ai Funghi and Linguine allo Scoglio, alongside a variety of artisan pizzas and rosemary-roasted rib-eye steak.

This is the perfect choice for a relaxed weekend lunch on the terrace or a cozy, authentic Italian dinner that feels like a home-cooked meal.

name: Cafe Murano Bermondsey
list_view_snippet: Angela Hartnett’s sophisticated neighbourhood gem serving refined Italian classics and small-batch wines in a bright, open-kitchen setting in the heart of Bermondsey.
full_profile:
Cafe Murano Bermondsey is a sophisticated neighbourhood gem from chef Angela Hartnett. The interior is anchored by a vibrant open kitchen and sleek dining counters that offer a front-row seat to the culinary action and the bustle of the street outside. It successfully blends the elegance of a city brasserie with the warmth of a local haunt, providing an approachable yet refined setting for all-day dining.

The menu focuses on authentic, seasonal Italian flavors with a distinct local flair. Alongside fresh antipasti, the kitchen serves elevated versions of regional classics like the signature Chicken Milanese and indulgent Osso Bucco Risotto. The beverage program is equally specialised, featuring a 100% Italian wine list sourced from smaller, independent winemakers and a frequently changing selection of limited-edition bottles.

Perfect for impressive business lunches or relaxed weekend brunches, it is the premier choice for diners seeking high-caliber Italian soul in a stylish, modern environment.

name: Casse-Croûte
list_view_snippet: An intimate, 25-seat slice of Paris on Bermondsey Street, serving a daily-changing menu of soul-warming, authentic French bistro classics.
full_profile:
Casse-Croûte is a masterclass in high-impact hospitality, delivering a 'garlic-breathed, Gallic bear hug' within its intimate 25-seat dining room. The setting is quintessentially French, featuring red leather banquettes, monochrome tiled floors, and paper tablecloths scrawled with handwritten reservations. By eschewing digital booking for a strictly phone-or-walk-in policy, the venue maintains an atmosphere of personal, old-school charm.

The kitchen, led by chef Sylvain Soulard, offers a seasonally inspired menu that changes daily based on market availability. Diners can expect masterfully executed classics such as lapin à la moutarde with luxurious, butter-rich mash or a creative quiche lorraine served with crispy Bayonne ham. The wine list is exclusively French, highlighting biodynamic selections and rare regional finds.

This is the 'instant smash' restaurant you always hope to find in France but rarely do. It is perfect for romantic dates or intimate group gatherings centered on reasonably priced, pleasure-driven food.

name: Chapter -72
list_view_snippet: A vibrant Bermondsey Street social hub blending speciality coffee with award-winning Espresso Martinis, craft beers, and artisan pastries in a cozy, welcoming setting.
full_profile:
Chapter -72 is a warm and cozy neighbourhood fixture located just around the corner from London Bridge Station. It serves as a calm, stylish sanctuary that transitions seamlessly from a bright morning cafe opening at 7:00 am into a boozy evening lounge. With its friendly staff and artistic coffee culture, it is the ideal spot for a relaxed catch-up or a quiet moment of reflection amidst the energetic heart of Bermondsey Street.

The culinary focus is split between expertly crafted speciality coffee and a creative bar program. While the daytime menu features fresh pastries and signature toasties, the venue is most famous for its 'best ever' Espresso Martinis, which are available in a variety of innovative and classic flavours. Craft beer enthusiasts are also well-catered for, and the shop even hosts interactive masterclasses for those looking to perfect their cocktail-making skills.

It is the perfect choice for early morning commuters seeking a high-quality caffeine fix or friends gathering for late-night cocktails and 'good vibes'.

name: Dockley Road
list_view_snippet: A neighbourhood favourite near Spa Terminus serving honest, unfussy dishes in a laid-back, community-focused setting.
full_profile:
Dockley Road is the kind of local restaurant every neighbourhood wishes it had: unpretentious, welcoming, and quietly confident in its cooking. The vibe is relaxed and family-friendly, with simple furnishings letting the food take centre stage.

The menu changes seasonally but stays rooted in modern European comfort food — think slow-cooked meats, fresh salads, and hearty mains that won’t break the bank. Portions are generous, flavours are clean.

Perfect for a midweek supper without the fuss. No gimmicks, just good food done properly.

name: Fleurie
list_view_snippet: A cozy French-style brasserie on Bermondsey Street serving seasonal small plates, curated bubbles, and signature cocktails in a warm, welcoming space.
full_profile:
Fleurie is an intimate French-style brasserie that brings a touch of continental charm to the heart of Bermondsey Street. Created and hosted by Simon and Sophie, the venue prides itself on a warm, personal greeting that makes every guest feel immediately at home. The atmosphere is designed for conviviality and relaxed conversation, offering a small but vibrant sanctuary for those who value personal hospitality.

The culinary focus is centered on seasonal small plates, meticulously prepared and ideal for sharing across the table. To accompany the fare, the bar offers a carefully chosen selection of wines and bubbles, alongside 'lip-smackingly great' cocktails crafted for the discerning palate. The menu is intentionally concise, allowing the kitchen to prioritise the freshest seasonal ingredients and bold flavour profiles.

This neighbourhood gem is best for relaxed group sharing or an intimate evening centered on fine bubbles and artisanal cocktails.

name: Flour & Grape
list_view_snippet: A no-booking pasta and wine bar serving handmade noodles, natural wines, and a lively basement bar with its own Spotify playlist.
full_profile:
Flour & Grape is exactly what it sounds like: a love letter to pasta and wine. The front-of-house is bright and bustling, with counter seating overlooking the open kitchen. Downstairs, a moodier bar space plays host to late-night spritzes and good conversation.

The pasta is made fresh daily — expect silky tagliatelle, pillowy gnocchi, and standout ravioli. Gluten-free options are available, and the 'Treat Hour' offers exceptional value. The wine list leans natural and low-intervention, perfectly matching the carb-heavy feast.

No bookings accepted, so be prepared to queue — it’s worth it. Perfect for casual dates or catching up with friends over a carafe of orange wine. Come hungry.

name: Hakata Ramen + Bar
list_view_snippet: Tonkotsu ramen, vegan options, and an izakaya basement bar in Bermondsey’s most comforting Japanese spot.
full_profile:
Down a quiet Bermondsey street, Hakata Ramen + Bar serves the ultimate comfort food: rich, creamy tonkotsu broth made from slow-boiled pork bones. The ground floor is bright and casual, but downstairs reveals a buzzing izakaya-style bar perfect for sake and small bites.

Customisation is key — choose your noodle firmness, spice level, and toppings. Vegan ramen is equally satisfying, with a plant-based broth that doesn’t compromise on depth. Add gyoza or karaage chicken on the side.

Best for solo dinners, quick lunches, or groups grabbing a bowl before heading to the bar downstairs. Affordable, fast, and deeply satisfying.

name: José Tapas Bar
list_view_snippet: A legendary no-booking tapas bar from José Pizarro, serving sherry, jamón, and daily blackboard specials.
full_profile:
José Tapas Bar is a Bermondsey institution — a tiny, perpetually busy spot where standing room only is part of the charm. The narrow space hums with energy, counter seats filled with locals and sherry glasses.

The menu changes daily, written on a blackboard above the bar. Expect perfectly salty jamón, grilled octopus, tortilla española, and whatever seasonal produce José’s team found that morning. The sherry list is exceptional, and the attached Spanish wine shop means you can take a bottle home.

No reservations, no fuss — just exceptional tapas. Dog-friendly and wonderfully authentic. Best for a quick solo bite, a first date, or an impromptu catch-up where you don’t mind standing.

name: Lolo
list_view_snippet: An all-day European café with outdoor seating, counter dining, and a casual-chic vibe from breakfast to dinner.
full_profile:
Lolo is Bermondsey’s all-day answer to 'where shall we go?' — bright by day, softly lit by night. The space feels effortlessly stylish yet relaxed, with communal tables and kitchen counter seating for watching the action.

Breakfast means pastries and good coffee; lunch brings salads and tartines; dinner shifts to small plates and natural wines. The menu is European-leaning, seasonal, and never overcomplicated. Think burrata with roasted peppers, slow-cooked lamb shoulder, and a terrific crème brûlée.

Perfect for a solo breakfast with a book, a working lunch, or a laid-back dinner with friends. No need to over-plan — Lolo works for almost any occasion.

name: Pedro's Wine Bar
list_view_snippet: An independent Portuguese wine merchant and bar specialising in hidden gems, expert knowledge, and home delivery.
full_profile:
Pedro’s isn’t just a wine bar — it’s a passion project. This independent Portuguese merchant focuses on small-producer, hard-to-find wines from the Douro, Alentejo, and beyond. The space is intimate and knowledge-packed, with Pedro himself often on hand to guide your choice.

There’s no full kitchen, but the focus is squarely on the wine. Expect exceptional by-the-glass options, tasting flights, and a retail selection you won’t find elsewhere. Cheese and charcuterie are available to accompany.

Best for wine lovers, curious drinkers, and anyone tired of supermarket staples. Delivery available across London.

name: Pique-Nique
list_view_snippet: A rustic, park-side French rotisserie in a converted pavilion, serving succulent roasted meats and decadent sharing plates to a local, laid-back crowd.
full_profile:
Pique-Nique is a charming sibling to Casse-Croûte, uniquely set within a converted pavilion in the heart of Tanner Street Park. It offers a rustic and relaxed neighbourhood retreat away from the main street's energy, featuring an atmosphere that feels both intimate and communal.

The menu specialises in the French rôtisserie tradition, with high-quality meats designed specifically for sharing. Diners can enjoy signature dishes such as Chateaubriand and Veal en Croute, alongside more delicate sweet options like their celebrated banana soufflé.

This park-side gem is highly recommended for leisurely weekend brunches or a traditional Sunday roast with family. It is the perfect choice for those seeking a sophisticated yet unpretentious French meal in a serene, leafy setting.

name: Pizarro Restaurant
list_view_snippet: José Pizarro’s flagship Bermondsey restaurant serving suckling pig, Spanish wines, and private dining in a converted warehouse.
full_profile:
Housed in a stunning converted warehouse on Bermondsey Street, Pizarro Restaurant is José Pizarro’s love letter to Spanish fine dining. The space is warm and industrial — exposed brick, dark wood, and soft lighting — with a private dining room for special occasions.

The menu goes beyond tapas into proper Spanish gastronomy. Signature suckling pig (cochinillo) is a must-order — impossibly crisp skin, meltingly tender meat. There’s also exceptional jamón, fresh seafood, and a Spanish wine list that runs deep. Large group bookings are welcome, and the semi-private space works perfectly for celebrations.

Best for milestone dinners, client entertaining, or any night you want to linger over rioja and roasted meats. It’s special without being stiff.

name: Restaurant Story
list_view_snippet: A two-Michelin-starred tasting menu experience telling seasonal British stories through inventive, narrative-driven dishes.
full_profile:
Restaurant Story is fine dining with a soul — and two Michelin stars to prove it. Overlooking Tower Bridge, the dining room is elegant but not intimidating, with floor-to-ceiling windows flooding the space with light. Every dish tells a story, inspired by chef Tom Sellers’ memories and British seasons.

The tasting menu is the only option, and it’s an unfolding narrative: from a candle that melts into beef dripping to a dish inspired by a childhood packed lunch. Seasonal, local, and deeply creative — this is dining as theatre. Service is warm and knowledgeable, never stuffy.

Reservations essential. Best for serious food lovers, anniversaries, or any occasion where you want to be genuinely surprised. Allow three hours and trust the team. Worth every penny.

name: Sentosa
list_view_snippet: A warm Bermondsey gem offering an authentic journey through Singapore and Malaysia with imported spices, heritage-led recipes, and signature chili crab.
full_profile:
Sentosa is a warm and friendly sanctuary on Bermondsey Street that invites guests on a genuine culinary journey through Singapore and Malaysia. Founded by Ivan Lee to fill a gap in London’s authentic Asian scene, the space is welcoming and unpretentious, designed to evoke the happy memories and vibrant aromas of the Malay Peninsula.

The kitchen is powered by seven talented chefs from Singapore, Malaysia and Indonesia who utilise herbs and ingredients imported directly from Singapore to maintain traditional standards. Signature dishes include the sweet and savoury Singapore chilli crab served with soft, steamed buns and the perfectly balanced Malaysia Boleh Nasi Lemak, featuring fragrant coconut rice and spicy chilli squid.

Dedicated to high-quality service and authentic flavours, Sentosa is the ultimate choice for food lovers seeking the true soul of Singaporean and Malaysian cooking. It is perfect for casual dinners or those looking for a sophisticated, heritage-driven Asian experience.

name: Tanner & Co
list_view_snippet: A heritage gastro-bar with bottomless brunch, a cocktail bar, and an industrial warehouse vibe in Bermondsey.
full_profile:
Tanner & Co transforms a former leather tannery into a sprawling, industrial-chic pub and dining room. Exposed brick, leather banquettes, and a long bar set the scene for everything from morning coffee to late-night cocktails.

The food is British comfort done right: Sunday roasts with a carvery trolley, bottomless brunch on weekends, and hearty mains like beer-battered fish and chips. The warehouse space doubles as an events venue, so expect a lively buzz.

Cocktails are serious — try the espresso martini — and the beer list leans local. Perfect for group bookings, birthday brunches, or a lazy Sunday afternoon with friends. Heritage charm without the pretension.

name: Texas Joe's
list_view_snippet: An authentic, high-energy Texas smokehouse serving the 'best BBQ in town' with a focus on slow-smoked meats and casual, no-booking-needed hospitality.
full_profile:
Texas Joe’s captures a casual and high-energy spirit, functioning as a dedicated smokehouse that prides itself on being the 'best BBQ in town'. The atmosphere is unpretentious and straightforward, designed for diners who prioritize authentic flavour and a relaxed, rustic setting. It serves as a bustling neighbourhood anchor where the vibe is defined by the energy of a traditional pit-led eatery.

The culinary focus is squarely on traditional Texas-style barbecue, featuring slow-cooked meats that emphasise deep, smoky profiles and traditional seasonings. Occupying a mid-range price band, the offerings are designed to be accessible, hearty, and satisfying. Every dish reflects a commitment to the 'slow-and-low' philosophy, ensuring the tender textures and robust barks that characterise high-quality Southern barbecue.

This is the ultimate destination for meat enthusiasts seeking a satisfying, no-fuss meal in Bermondsey. It is exceptionally well-suited for spontaneous walk-ins or organised group feasts, thanks to a welcoming policy that specifically accommodates reservations for parties of six or more.

name: The Garrison
list_view_snippet: A classic Bermondsey Street pub serving solid British food, local ales, and a warm neighbourhood welcome.
full_profile:
The Garrison is everything a great London pub should be: wood-panelled, softly lit, and full of locals. It sits proudly on Bermondsey Street, serving well-kept cask ales and a British menu that doesn’t try too hard — and that’s its charm.

Think Scotch eggs, fish and chips, steak and ale pie. Quality ingredients, generous portions, and a wine list that punches above its weight. The service is friendly and efficient, and there are gift vouchers available for regulars.

Best for a quiet pint, a Sunday roast with the family, or a midweek meal when you want reliability and warmth. No bookings needed most nights.

name: The Last Talisman
list_view_snippet: An Asian fusion cocktail bar with a hidden hibachi grill, late-night energy, and a magical weekend brunch.
full_profile:
The Last Talisman is Bermondsey’s most theatrical dining experience — a dark, moody space filled with neon, lush greenery, and hidden corners. Downstairs, the Mala Madre events space hosts private parties and live DJs.

The menu roams across Asia: hibachi-grilled skewers, bao buns, curries, and wok-tossed noodles. Cocktails are the real showstoppers — smoky, spicy, and served with flair. Weekend brunch has a 'magical' theme (think theatrical presentation and bottomless options).

The mezzanine offers semi-private dining, perfect for birthdays or date night with a twist. Late-night, the bar fills with a young, energetic crowd. Best for after-work drinks that turn into dancing, or a brunch that feels like a night out. Book ahead.

name: The Woolpack
list_view_snippet: A dog-friendly Bermondsey Street pub with an epic garden, outdoor seating, and classic British pub food.
full_profile:
The Woolpack is the sort of pub you wish was your local — a charming Bermondsey Street spot with a huge, sun-trap garden that’s absolute gold in summer. Inside, it’s cosy and traditional; outside, it’s a leafy escape from the city.

The menu sticks to British classics: burgers, pies, Sunday roasts, and a decent fish finger sandwich. Dogs are welcome (water bowls and biscuits provided), and there are gift vouchers for loyal regulars. The beer selection includes local Bermondsey brewers.

Best for summer afternoons with a cold pint, casual family lunches, or a dog walk that conveniently ends at the bar. No fuss, just good times.

name: Trivet Restaurant
list_view_snippet: A sophisticated European restaurant and wine bar with a terrace, tasting club, and Casual Mondays for walk-ins.
full_profile:
Trivet is Bermondsey’s quietly elegant all-rounder — a European restaurant with a serious wine bar attached. The dining room is understated and refined, with a terrace for al fresco meals and a wine cellar for deeper exploration.

The à la carte menu changes seasonally, but signatures include perfectly cooked fish, slow-roasted meats, and exceptional pasta. Casual Mondays offer a more relaxed walk-in experience, while the Tasting Club digs into rare vintages. The wine list is award-worthy, curated by a team who genuinely love natural and classic pours.

Best for a sophisticated date night, a business dinner that impresses without shouting, or a weekend lunch on the terrace. Private dining available.

name: WatchHouse
list_view_snippet: Bermondsey’s original WatchHouse serves modern speciality coffee, pastries, and brews in a character-filled space.
full_profile:
WatchHouse is the house that started it all — the original Bermondsey location of London’s cult speciality coffee brand. The space is small (seats just ten), full of character, and always smells of freshly roasted beans.

The brew bar offers pour-overs, espressos, and batch brews from rotating microlots. Pastries are fresh, simple, and perfectly paired. It’s dog-friendly, so expect a furry companion or two.

Best for a quiet morning coffee with a book, a quick catch-up with a fellow coffee nerd, or a takeaway flat white that actually tastes of something. No laptops, no fuss — just exceptional coffee.
